reviews.title: Future of Work OS
reviews.text: ClickUp has become the operating system for my work. What I like most about ClickUp is how everything comes together in one place. The UI is clean, the platform is genuinely enjoyable to use, and it has helped me simplify and better manage my overall tech stack. The AI agent functionality is especially impressive. The onboarding experience was also strong. Their team was supportive during the initial setup, and once I understood how ClickUp works, I stopped feeling like I constantly needed to learn another new tool. The main thing I would improve is the screen recording functionality. I would love the ability to record my camera at the same time as my screen, similar to Loom. That would make it even easier to replace another tool in my stack. Overall, ClickUp is solving one of the biggest problems I had, tool sprawl. Instead of having work scattered across different platforms, it gives my team and my AI a shared source of context. That improves visibility, reduces the chances of missed deadlines, and makes execution much easier. It is increasingly replacing the need for separate tools like Slack, Loom, and parts of Zoom for me. I am very happy with the platform and especially excited about the direction ClickUp is taking with AI.

reviews.text: I've been the lead admin for ClickUp at our agency, responsible for the entire workspace setup — custom fields, permissions, automations, dashboards, and recurring task logic — and overall it's been a very positive experience. That said, the learning curve is steep if you're setting things up from scratch without much guidance. I had to build our own onboarding materials (videos, slides, a knowledge base) just to get the rest of the team comfortable, because ClickUp's own onboarding didn't cover the more advanced configuration options in enough depth. Automations are powerful but can behave unpredictably if you're not careful with triggers, and some permission settings aren't as intuitive as they should be for teams with junior and senior roles mixed together. Overall, if you have the time (or a dedicated person) to configure it properly, ClickUp becomes an extremely capable tool. It's not plug-and-play, but the payoff is worth it.

reviews.title: AI Without Context Is Just Bad Code
reviews.text: AI without context is basically a function with no parameters. It might run, but the output is going to be generic. That’s the problem with how a lot of teams are using AI today. They have access to powerful models, but those models are disconnected from the actual work: the tasks, docs, goals, dashboards, priorities, dependencies, and conversations that define how the team operates. In developer terms, it’s like calling: generateProductivity(); …and expecting magic. But real productivity comes when AI has access to the right inputs: generateProductivity({ tasks, docs, goals, dashboards, teamContext, priorities, workflows }); That’s what makes a Converged AI Workspace different. It’s not just an AI chat window bolted onto your stack. It’s AI embedded natively into the environment where work already happens. When AI is bolted on, it has no real runtime context. When AI is built in, it can understand the full application state. That’s the difference with ClickUp Brain. It doesn’t just sit on top of your work like a third-party plugin. It lives inside the workspace, with native access to tasks, docs, dashboards, goals, and integrations across the tools your team already uses. So every AI interaction is powered by real context: your data, your structure, your priorities, and your workflows. Because AI isn’t the future of work by itself. Contextual AI is. Or to put it another way: if (AI.hasContext()) { return betterDecisions + fasterExecution + fewerContextSwitches; } How much more could your AI do if it actually knew your work?

reviews.title: Flexible, powerful and worth the investment
reviews.text: Overall, ClickUp has been a really positive experience. In less than six months it became the backbone of our team's project management and the single source of truth for almost the entire operation. What stands out the most is the flexibility, the hierarchy of Spaces, Folders and Lists combined with multiple views and customizable fields adapts to whatever workflow we throw at it, without forcing us into someone else's method. The UX is intuitive enough that I got up to speed on my own, and the robust API plus native integrations with tools like Gmail and Outlook make it easy to plug ClickUp into the rest of our stack. ClickUp Brain is a nice bonus when I remember to use it. It's not perfect, of course. Paying in dollars from Brazil hurts the budget and is the kind of thing you have to justify internally every time you expand the team. The notification volume can get noisy until you tune it properly, performance shows some lag in heavier workspaces, and the lack of Portuguese support adds friction when you need to talk to the support team, although when I did reach out, the experience was smooth and they solved my issue quickly. In the end, it's a tool that delivers a lot for what it charges. It replaced several scattered tools, brought clarity to our operation and centralized everything we need in one place. I'd recommend it to any team looking to stop juggling spreadsheets and chats and finally have real visibility over their work.
